items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jomo Kenyatta, when he was released from jail in Kenya after ten years – and they were going to kill him, but the people threatened such revolt that they let him live – but after ten years, when he was released, all the white people who had settled in Kenya says, “Are you going to persecute us now?”

ctx.x: Okay, but how did we attract that to ourselves as a people?

So where’s the laziness? Jomo Kenyatta, when he was released from jail in Kenya after ten years – and they were going to kill him, but the people threatened such revolt that they let him live – but after ten years, when he was released, all the white people who had settled in Kenya says, “Are you going to persecute us now?” He said, “No.” That’s why we went through the persecution that we went through. Because we persecuted people before. So we brought it back to ourselves. Because there is a law. As it says in…
The slaveholders never considered themselves evil. They considered themselves benevolent people. They will tell you, “We treated our slaves wonderfully.”
